rationale: A wins because it keeps the skepticism attached to the evidence: "An unprofitable Rivian is turning its charging network into a revenue line — the question is whether it's enough to matter" is a real business angle, not a victory lap. B has useful bones, but "Wall Street hasn't repriced it yet" invents market behavior the update never gave us. That is how a decent angle set picks up a preventable limp.
gaps_in_A: "Rivian fields a rival to Tesla's Supercharger network" overstates the competitive proof; the update supports open access and NACS plugs, not that Rivian is fielding a true rival at Tesla scale.
"following the industry's shift away from automaker-exclusive plugs" needs outside sourcing before it can be asserted as the frame; A flags that proof need, but the headline still leans on it.
The consumer angle says the access change is "live now" through the app, but the actual app flow, compatible vehicles, and pricing numbers are all still missing.
gaps_in_B: "Wall Street hasn't repriced it yet" is invented. No stock movement, analyst reaction, valuation data, or market-pricing evidence appears in the update.
Angles 1 and 4 are padded cousins: "calls it a revenue stream" and "charging-network operator" are both finance/investor framings until analyst evidence makes the valuation version distinct.
"because it needs income" is too confident. Rivian is not yet profitable, but the update does not prove this move was made out of financial necessity.
"After Tesla" and "Tesla opening its Supercharger network was a major structural story" rely on outside context as a premise instead of treating it as proof to gather.
